notes: DCA 6-2015 Table B1, Post Heights Based on Tributary Area for Corner Posts (Appendix B, p. B3), transcribed 2026-09-27 (#42 slice B3) from the PDF in the guide's sources, read from the page rendered at 500 dpi in four crops and checked against the text extraction; both agree on all 250 cells. Appendix B offers Tables B1 through B3 'As an alternative to Table 4' (p. B2); napkin uses them for its end posts, the corner posts of Figure B1 (p. B1). Each row is one printed cell: a species group heading × the 6x6 or 4x4 Post Height (ft.) column × a Tributary Area (sq. ft.) row, an upper-bound band of the area (the page prints no lower bound; the domain's min, 1 sq ft, is napkin's). A height is whole feet as printed; a cell printed NP is 'notPermitted': true and is answered Out of scope quoting NP (the page does not expand it). Species groups are the five headings as printed; 'SPF' is the guide's Spruce-Pine-Fir, which note 2, whose superscript sits on SPF, spells 'spruce-pine-fir'. Notes 1 and 3 sit on the title's 'Based', so apply to every row; note 2 sits on Douglas Fir-Larch, Hem-Fir and SPF in the headings, so rides on the rows of their three groups. Every note is verbatim and shown with results (not-encoded). Not yet reviewed: docs/code-packs/reviews/us-ct-2022/dca6-tableB1.md.

footnotes.text: Assumes No 2. Stress grade and wet service conditions.
Incising assumed for Douglas fir-larch, hem-fir, and spruce-pine-fir.

Some post heights for 4x4 post sizes show a greater load carrying capacity than 6x6 post sizes since different ASTM Standards are used to develop design values for visually graded dimension lumber vs. visually graded timbers.
